title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, report the bootstrap CI as a descriptive secondary summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not specified in the frozen preregistration), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises operational gains but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior literature documents LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so that any paired difference is attributable only to deterministic validation and the permitted repair.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and controlled studies in LLMs document frequent hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that reduce correctness for code and configuration tasks [1],[2]. Work on constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning shows gains for executable outputs in structured domains, though much evidence originates outside NetOps and thus depends on validator fidelity when transferred to networking contexts [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers emphasize verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and protocol‑based governance; these present prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and external enforcement rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements this literature by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and at‑most‑one repair when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. This avoids conflating downstream interventions with first‑pass prompt/decoding differences.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Therefore, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). The design does not measure effects attributable to independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat. The declared provider/model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a digital‑twin validator that enforces workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus, selection rule, and scoring. Tasks were selected deterministically using the preregistered ordinal rule producing exactly 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels. The validator compares parsed candidate command sequences against manifest constraints and emits structured validator traces archived per episode; scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary validity outcome required by the paired analysis.

Execution accounting, retries, and missingness. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. The analysis executor applied the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5) and no failed hosted calls.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table is n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Confirmatory hierarchy and bootstrap nuance (requested clarification). The exact two‑sided McNemar is the preregistered confirmatory analysis and remains primary; it did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was a preregistered descriptive secondary summary and equals [0.001, 0.01]. That bootstrap interval can exclude zero despite a non‑significant exact two‑sided McNemar because percentile bootstrap intervals over paired resamples are sensitive to extremely sparse discordant counts: with only five discordant pairs (n10=5, n01=0), resampling variability and the discrete support of the paired difference can produce a percentile bound that does not include zero even though the exact permutation‑based paired test yields a two‑sided p above 0.05. Any one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline, p = 0.03125) was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration and is therefore reported as exploratory/post‑hoc; it does not replace the preregistered confirmatory inference.

Repairs and representative traces. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred; representative episode artifacts show the validator rejecting initial candidates for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call, and the validator accepting the repaired candidate after revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived in the execution bundle. Total model calls used = 1005.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms began from the same sampled initial candidate, the observed paired improvement (0.005) can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the limited repair budget; it does not measure effects that would accrue from different first‑pass generations, prompt engineering, or constrained decoding. The small absolute gain and the preregistered null confirmatory result reflect three interacting factors evident in the archived artifacts: very high baseline validity (0.995) producing few discordant pairs, a small number of repair invocations (5), and validator scope that deterministically enforces the manifested constraints.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: safe‑deploy depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity: synthetic corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments and other model families. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline reduces discordant counts and the sensitivity of paired exact tests relative to preregistered power assumptions (which had assumed baseline ≈ 0.60).

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in this synthetic workflow setting, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups supported by the archive include: (1) independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding effects; (2) repair budget sweeps to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expanded validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should include power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates and frozen analysis plans.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only and does not measure differences from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms (those were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains.
Sparse repairs: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified.
